newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, despite cold, crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, despite cold, crude.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil took some comfort on Thursday from the cold snap gripping much of Europe and stronger crude futures, but prices were steady with the exception of barges.
Dealers said high sulphur barges traded around $118 and $119 a tonne fob ARA for much of the day.
"Demand has been good with shippers coming into the market and having to pay for prompt barrels," said one barge trader.

But, despite the firmer tone cargo levels were broadly unchanged. Market players said the market was still not liquid enough for representative trade and even the paper market was muted. "I don't see any great demand out there," said one.
A Scandinavian cargo loading Jan 8-10 was understood to be looking for floating numbers. Traders said they were uncertain whether a major's cargo was to be offered or taken into own system.

The low sulphur cargo market was also slow with the main Med buyer still out of the market. Traders said Jan paper levels of $124.75-$125.50 fob NWE reflected the wet market. A 25,000 tonne Danish cargo loading Jan 17-20 was offered at $124 fob, but had received no bids. A 50,000 tonne Swedish cargo was also unsuccesful in attracting interest.
